It is fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 (the fix changes html/render.go), and the Go vulnerability database names the parser functions Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and parser.parse as the vulnerable functions: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5027, https://go.dev/issue/79572, https://go.dev/cl/781701, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8 Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and with -ldflags -s -w, as their Go build information records, so their functions were read from each binary's Go function table (pclntab), which lists runtime.main in every binary. Every binary was also searched as raw bytes for the package-qualified names, which also finds functions the compiler inlined. golang.org/x/net is v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.52.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.53.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.55.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, and v0.56.0 to v0.62.0 in every later build (v0.62.0 from 0.34.1-r5), as listed in the Go build information of both programs. The binaries in builds 0.31.1-r0 to 0.34.2-r1 contain no golang.org/x/net/html function or package-qualified name at all. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search, run on a test program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -ldflags -s -w for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0 and golang.org/x/net v0.53.0, which calls html.Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and Render, finds (*parser).parse, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and Render in the function table and all four Parse names and Render in the byte search.

CVE-2026-42502 (GO-2026-5027): the golang.org/x/net/html parser mishandled HTML elements in foreign content, so parsing arbitrary HTML and rendering it with Render can produce an unexpected tree, which can be used for XSS against applications that sanitize HTML before rendering it. The vulnerable code is Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the parser's parse method in the golang.org/x/net/html package (the functions GO-2026-5027 lists), fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5027, https://go.dev/issue/79572, https://go.dev/cl/781701, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8. We read every published build-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64 (2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only), after verifying each download against its index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times for each architecture in the package index; the one copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one program, the Go frontend program /usr/bin/build, besides the apk metadata. For every Go program in every build we read the function table (pclntab) and searched the binary's strings; each program's function table contains runtime.main. No build contains golang.org/x/net/html code: the golang.org/x/net packages linked into /usr/bin/build are http/httpguts, http2, http2/hpack, idna, internal/timeseries and trace, and none of the parser functions above appears in its function table or its strings. As a check, the same function-table reader lists ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the parser's parse method, and the same strings search finds all five names, in a test program built against golang.org/x/net v0.54.0 for x86_64 and aarch64. The vulnerable code is not present, so the golang.org/x/net version recorded in the build information does not make this package affected.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-42502 (GO-2026-5027): parsing arbitrary HTML with golang.org/x/net/html and rendering it with Render could produce an unexpected HTML tree when elements were fostered under foreign content, which can be used for XSS in applications that sanitize HTML before rendering it. It is fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 by commit a8fb2fe (CL 781701, which names CVE-2026-42502): https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5027, https://go.dev/issue/79572, https://go.dev/cl/781701, https://github.com/golang/net/commit/a8fb2fe4f737, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8. The Go vulnerability database lists the vulnerable functions as Parse, ParseFragment, ParseFragmentWithOptions, ParseWithOptions and parser.parse in golang.org/x/net/html. This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. We read every package built from the golang-1.26-dev source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository and its security repository: golang-1.26-dev (15 builds, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1), golang-1.26-dev-oci-config (15 builds, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1), golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config (15 builds, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, all in the security repository) and golang-1.26-dev-doc (15 builds, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1), each for x86_64 and aarch64 and each matching its index checksum, with a full listing that includes symlinks. The Go source tree it ships vendors these golang.org/x/net packages for the standard library, per src/vendor/modules.txt: dns/dnsmessage, http/httpguts, http/httpproxy, http2/hpack, idna, lif, nettest; src/cmd/vendor/modules.txt lists no golang.org/x/net package. golang.org/x/net/html is not among them, and no file or symlink path in any package names golang.org/x/net/html. We read the Go function table (pclntab) and the ELF symbol table of every ELF file in every package (the go and gofmt commands, the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool and the prebuilt .syso object files): none contains a golang.org/x/net/html name. A byte search of every file in every package, which also catches the names of inlined functions and any vendored source, finds the string golang.org/x/net/html only in /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/go/internal/list/list.go and /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/go/alldocs.go, where it is an example package path in the go list help text, and in the go command (/usr/lib/go/bin/go), which embeds that help text. As a positive control, the same readers and byte search find golang.org/x/net/html.Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and (*parser).parse in a test program we built against golang.org/x/net v0.54.0, a release before the fix, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/net/html takes it from its own golang.org/x/net requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/net in that program.
